newsitem.title: USA: Justice approves First Virginia, Premier merger.
newsitem.headline: Justice approves First Virginia, Premier merger.

text.p: The Justice Department said Tuesday it would permit First Virginia Banks Inc. and Premier Bankshares Corp to merge if they sell three branches in southwestern Virginia.
The merger would also have to be approved by the Federal Reserve Board.
"By selling the offices -- with total deposits of about $44.3 million -- the companies will resolve antitrust concerns," the Justice Department announced.

Acting Assistant Attorney General Joel Klein said that the merger had presented a "significant risk" to consumers in southwestern Virginia. He said the consumers "rely on competition to ensure they can get loans at the lowest possible interest rates and better services."

First virginia is based in Falls Church, Va., and has 358 offices with about $7 billion in deposits and $8.2 billion in total assets. Premier is based in Bluefield, Va., with 36 offices and $650 milion in total deposit as part of $744 million in total assets.
